NC-2025E1-SR1.title: Senate Rules - 2026 First Extra Session.
NC-2025E1-SR1.policyArea: ADOPTED; GENERAL ASSEMBLY; RESOLUTIONS, HOUSE & SENATE, SIMPLE; RULES
NC-2025E1-SR1.aiSummary: This resolution adopts the permanent rules for the North Carolina Senate for the 2026 First Extra Session. It sets rules for committee size and quorum, how bills are filed and assigned, and what kinds of bills and resolutions may be taken up in the session. It also makes clear that the resolution takes effect when adopted.

NC-2025-SB445.aiSummary: The act changes several state rules on local planning, school testing surveys, and redevelopment. It would change how long some local land-use rights last, limit when local governments can change approved development plans, and set rules for certain uses on redevelopment land. It also lets students take surveys tied to a college admissions test with parent consent and requires notice to parents of 11th graders.

NC-2025-HB206.aiSummary: The law makes several changes to public safety and victim help programs in North Carolina. It lets the Department of Public Safety and the Air National Guard sign a new 50-year land use license for part of the Stanly County Airport, and it allows state disaster-response trailers and utility vehicles to be given to local governments, nonprofits, or survivors needing long-term housing help. It raises some crime victim compensation limits, changes claim rules and privacy sharing, and lets tribal police chiefs enter mutual aid agreements with other law enforcement agencies. It also changes how the Adjutant General is appointed and confirmed by the Governor and the General Assembly.

NC-2025-HB1126.aiSummary: North Carolina enacted a bill with technical and clarifying changes to the State Treasurer laws and to the rules for a legislative oversight commission. It gives that commission broader access to records, data, buildings, and some payroll systems from state, local, and some public-funded entities, and it keeps certain information confidential. It also makes it a Class 2 misdemeanor to hide, destroy, change, or refuse to provide required material to the commission.

NC-2025-HB198.aiSummary: The bill would change how profits from the Town of Angier ABC Board are split. It would send 10% to recreation programs in Angier, let 10% be used for alcohol education and rehab work, and send the rest to the town’s general fund, with up to 25% of that share able to go to recreation. Any old funds held for the Angier Community Library would instead go to recreation programs in town.

It would also let the Secretary of State receive advance health care directives filed online. The bill would change the rules for qualified witnesses and update the standard form and instructions for these documents.
